s1.syndrome_frame: Asymptomatic hypopigmented skin lesions with gradual coalescence
salient_findings: Multiple round, hypopigmented macules on face and neck
Absence of hair growth in affected areas
key_facts: Male patient in his 40s
2-year history of skin lesions
Lesions first appeared on cheeks
Lesions have gradually coalesced
Lesion size ranges from 2-3 mm to 25 mm in diameter
No symptoms reported
Previous treatment for tinea versicolor was unsuccessful
Histopathologic findings show plate-like subepidermal tumor
Neoplastic cords consist of clear/pale epithelial cells with glycogen accumulation
Marked elastosis observed in dermis surrounding tumor

shortlist.label: Idiopathic guttate hypomelanosis
shortlist.why_kept: Matches clinical presentation of asymptomatic, hypopigmented macules with gradual coalescence

shortlist.label: Nevus depigmentosus
shortlist.why_kept: Consistent with congenital or acquired hypopigmented lesions, potentially matching the patient's presentation

shortlist.label: Pityriasis alba
shortlist.why_kept: Common condition presenting with hypopigmented patches, although typically with mild scaling and pruritus

shortlist.label: Vitiligo
shortlist.why_kept: Characterized by acquired, asymptomatic, hypopigmented macules, but often with a more rapid progression and potential for widespread involvement

shortlist.label: Nevus sebaceus
shortlist.why_kept: Rare, congenital lesion that can present as a hypopigmented macule, with potential for gradual growth and coalescence

raw.rationale: The histopathologic findings of a plate-like subepidermal tumor with neoplastic cords consisting of clear/pale epithelial cells and marked elastosis in the dermis surrounding the tumor are characteristic of Nevus sebaceus.

rejected.label: Nevus depigmentosus
rejected.why: Typically presents as a single, well-defined hypopigmented patch, not multiple lesions

rejected.label: Pityriasis alba
rejected.why: Usually presents with ill-defined, faintly hypopigmented patches and scaling, not characteristic of this case

rejected.label: Vitiligo
rejected.why: Typically presents with well-defined, depigmented patches, often with a history of trauma or autoimmune disorders, not consistent with this case
